name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text: To achieve our goal of recalling by meaning and building the brain graph, I propose we start by identifying and grouping related concepts, creating a mental framework to organize our thoughts. This approach allows us to establish connections between elements, making it easier to embed unembedded information and strengthen our memory. By doing so, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially investing more time upfront to create this framework, but it will pay off in the long run by improving our ability to recall information by meaning. This decision aligns with our quality-first principle, ensuring a solid foundation for our memory-building process.

name: Prune
text: I'm not convinced that grouping related concepts is the best starting point, as it may lead to overly broad categories and miss crucial nuances between elements. A more effective approach might be to focus on identifying key relationships and patterns between individual elements, allowing us to build a more detailed and accurate brain graph. This argument could be settled by testing both methods with a small set of elements and comparing the resulting graphs for clarity, completeness, and usefulness.
